title: Poached Egg
description: Poached Egg is a classic preparation where fresh eggs are gently cooked in simmering water until the whites are delicately set while the yolk remains perfectly runny. A staple of professional kitchens, it is commonly served with toasted sourdough, seasonal vegetables, or as the centerpiece of Eggs Benedict.

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: 4 fresh large eggs (the fresher, the better)
2 tbsp white wine vinegar (or champagne vinegar for refinement)

ingredients.title: For serving (optional, restaurant-style plating)
items: Fresh herbs: chives, tarragon, or parsley

instruction.title: 1. Prepare the Poaching Liquid
steps: In a wide saucepan, bring water to a gentle simmer (82–85 °C / 180–185 °F).
Add vinegar and salt. The vinegar helps the egg white set quickly and neatly.

instruction.title: 2. Prepare the Eggs
steps: Crack each egg into a small ramekin or cup (to ensure no broken yolks).
Use the freshest eggs possible—firm whites wrap better around the yolk.

instruction.title: 3. Poach the Eggs
steps: Stir the simmering water gently to create a mild whirlpool (for one egg at a time).
Slide the egg carefully into the center of the whirlpool.
Cook for 2 ½ to 3 minutes until the white is set but the yolk is still runny.
Lift gently with a slotted spoon, and place on a paper towel to drain.

instruction.title: 4. Finishing Touch
steps: Trim ragged edges of the egg white for a clean restaurant presentation.
Plate on buttered sourdough with spinach or asparagus.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Plate on buttered sourdough with spinach or asparagus.
Poached eggs are central to Eggs Benedict, Florentine, or served atop seasonal vegetables.

chefTips: Egg freshness is critical: older eggs spread and won’t hold shape.
Temperature control ensures delicate whites and runny yolk.
Vinegar type: White wine vinegar gives a clean finish; champagne vinegar adds elegance.
Serving suggestion: Poached eggs are central to Eggs Benedict, Florentine, or served atop seasonal vegetables.
